source_text:
Ταῦτα δὲ πάντα βεβαιοῖ ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ πίστις: καὶ γὰρ αὐτὸς διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου οὕτως προσκαλεῖται ἡμᾶς: Δεῦτε, τέκνα, ἀκούσατέ μου, φόβον κυρίου διδάξω ὑμᾶς.
τίς ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος ὁ θέλων ζωήν, ἀγαπῶν ἡμέρας ἰδεῖν ἀγαθάς ;
παῦσον τὴν γλῶσσάν σου ἀπὸ κακοῦ, καὶ χείλη σου τοῦ μὴ λαλῆσαι δόλον.
ἔκκλινον ἀπὸ κακοῦ, καὶ ποίησον ἀγαθόν.
ζήτησον εἰρήνην, καὶ δίωξον αὐτήν:
ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους, καὶ ὦτα αὐτοῦ πρὸς δέησιν αὐτῶν: πρόσωπον δὲ κυρίου ἐπὶ ποιοῦντας κακά, τοῦ ἐξολεθρεῦσαι ἐκ γῆς τὸ μνημόσυνον αὐτῶν.
ἐκέκραξεν ὁ δίκαιος, καὶ ὁ κύριος εἰσήκουσεν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ ἐρύσατο αὐτόν.
Πολλαὶ αἱ μάστιγες τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ, τοὺς δὲ ἐλπίζοντας ἐπὶ κύριον ἔλεος κυκλώσει.
thought_title: Faith in Christ confirms all these commands
orientation: Clement has just finished a long series of moral exhortations to wives, children, and all who fear God, and now grounds them in the call of Christ through the Holy Spirit, quoting Psalm 33 (LXX) as the voice of Christ.
pass_a_gloss: And all these things the faith in Christ confirms: for indeed he himself through the Holy Spirit thus calls us: Come, children, listen to me, the fear of the Lord I will teach you. Who is the man who wants life, loving to see good days? Stop your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit. Turn away from evil, and do good. Seek peace, and pursue it: the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are toward their supplication: but the face of the Lord is upon those who do evil, to destroy from the earth the memory of them. The righteous man cried out, and the Lord heard him, and from all his afflictions he rescued him. Many are the scourges of the sinner, but those who hope in the Lord, mercy will surround.

choices.why: The verb means to make firm or establish; 'confirms' preserves the sense that faith in Christ validates and secures all the preceding moral instructions.
The compound verb has the force of summoning someone toward oneself; rendering it as 'calls us to himself' keeps the personal direction of Christ's invitation.

choices.term: παῦσον τὴν γλῶσσάν σου ἀπὸ κακοῦ
choices.why: The imperative with ἀπό indicates cessation from a source; 'stop your tongue from evil' is literal and preserves the bodily agency of the tongue.
The verb is intensive, meaning complete destruction; 'destroy utterly' conveys the force of the compound.
The noun refers to whips or lashes as instruments of punishment; 'scourges' keeps the concrete image of affliction.
The verb means to encircle; 'will surround' preserves the image of mercy encompassing those who hope in the Lord.

bible_refs.note: Δεῦτε, τέκνα, ἀκούσατέ μου, φόβον κυρίου διδάξω ὑμᾶς through ἔλεος κυκλώσει

pass_b_english: Faith in Christ confirms all these things. For Christ himself calls us through the Holy Spirit, and this is what he says:

“Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord. Who is the person who desires life, who loves to see good days? Stop your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit. Turn away from evil, and do good. Seek peace, and pursue it. The eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their supplication; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to destroy utterly the memory of them from the earth. The righteous one cried out, and the Lord heard him, and rescued him from all his afflictions. Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy will surround those who hope in the Lord” (Psalm 34:11-17; Psalm 32:10).

polish.changed: Clarified that Christ is the speaker who calls through the Holy Spirit, and kept the long quotation as one continuous divine speech so the reader can follow who is speaking and where the Scripture citation applies.

problems.source_quote: Πολλαὶ αἱ μάστιγες τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ, τοὺς δὲ ἐλπίζοντας ἐπὶ κύριον ἔλεος κυκλώσει.
problems.why: The citation covers only Psalm 34:11-19. The last line, 'Many are the scourges of the sinner…', is Psalm 32:10 LXX (31:10 in English Bibles), so the reference misses it.

fixed: wrong_scripture is real: last line renders Πολλαὶ αἱ μάστιγες etc., not part of Psalm 34, so added second citation; used English 32:10 not suggested 31:10 per brief modern-numbering rule (LXX 31:10 = English 32:10).

problems.source_quote: ἐκέκραξεν ὁ δίκαιος, καὶ ὁ κύριος εἰσήκουσεν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ ἐρύσατο αὐτόν. Πολλαὶ αἱ μάστιγες τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ, τοὺς δὲ ἐλπίζοντας ἐπὶ κύριον ἔλεος κυκλώσει.
problems.why: The quotation is Psalm 34:11-17, then Psalm 32:10. Verses 18-19 of Psalm 34 are not quoted; 34:19 is a different saying.
problems.ruling: The quote ends at 'ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ ἐρύσατο αὐτόν', which is Ps 34:17. The citation '34:11-19' overshoots into unquoted verses 18-19, so the reference is wrong.

fixed: wrong_scripture fixed: citation narrowed to Psalm 34:11-17 because the quotation ends at ἐκέκραξεν ὁ δίκαιος (=34:17) and does not include 34:18-19; Psalm 32:10 retained for Πολλαὶ αὁ μάστιγες etc.
